parsed.label: negative intensifier after 'so'
parsed.trigger_hypothesis: The neuron fires negatively when the token is an adjective or adverb that follows the word 'so' and intensifies it, describing an extreme degree.
parsed.output_hypothesis: The neuron's negative activation suppresses the generation of extreme intensifiers after 'so', perhaps to avoid hyperbolic or overly emotional language.
alternatives: The neuron detects the word 'so' followed by any adjective/adverb, regardless of meaning.
The neuron responds to any token that is a scalar adjective (like 'great', 'deep') in any context.
parsed.adapter_changes: State B+1 consistently amplifies the negative activation (makes it more negative) across strong windows, especially in emotional_chat contexts (W22, W23, W24). State A+1 and C+1 slightly reduce the negative magnitude. State D+1 has minimal effect.

proposed_tests.discriminates: 'so' followed by adjective at sentence end vs. middle
proposed_tests.b_text: It is so cold that I shivered.

proposed_tests.discriminates: 'so' + adjective with positive vs. negative sentiment
'so' + adjective in quoted speech vs. narrative
'so' + adjective after comma vs. directly after 'so'
proposed_tests.a_text: It was, so beautiful, to see.
proposed_tests.b_text: It was so beautiful to see.
